correctness.rationale: Every committee is uniquely decomposed into an increasing path of inclusion-maximal selected interval types, with subordinate labels assigned to the first containing maximal type. The equivalence of first ownership with not being contained in the preceding maximal type proves the transition coefficient exactly. The right-endpoint argument proves coverage gain; the max-plus count DP and empty-label convolution are bijective, and count-weighted backward sampling is uniform. A standalone independent brute-force comparison passed 1,167,656 exhaustive small instances and 5,000 random nonnegative weighted instances; 7,000 sample outputs were all optimal. Exhaustion is limited to finite test sizes, not the proof.

evidence: Cohen–Gonen (2019), Algorithm 1 eliminates intervals that are strict subsets; Algorithm 2 outputs one optimal set; Manurangsi–Sornat and Avramidis et al. (2026) cover more voting rules for optimization, not counting.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The apparently broader interval/Thiele algorithms answer a weaker output task (find an optimum), and cannot simply be counted over: nested and duplicate candidates yield distinct optima lost by pruning. Our count handles all such cases.

originality.rationale: The exact count-and-uniform-sampling statement is not implied by known optimization algorithms. Cohen–Gonen explicitly discard contained intervals, which is lossless for the optimal score but destroys multiplicity information. Janeczko–Faliszewski establish hardness of general CCAV counting and motivate uniform tie-breaking; recent VI Thiele results address winner determination. Related accessible mathematical claims and published research records were compared. Residual unindexed-equivalence risk remains.
residual_risks: Unindexed prior counting algorithms for maximum coverage by intervals or for consecutive-ones matrices may be equivalent after translation.
Literature search cannot prove absolute priority; none of the inspected sources purport to solve exact all-labeled-optima counting on VI profiles.

value.rationale: Exact tied-committee counting and unbiased tie-breaking are explicitly motivated in the 2023 multiwinner literature, where general CCAV counting is difficult. A correct count distinguishes label identities and redundant or nested winners that standard interval optimization prunes. The polynomial all-k recurrence makes exact, non-approximate fair tie-breaking available in a natural structured voting domain; this is stronger than routine recomputation of one optimum and is independent of any finite census.
